<objective>
Deliver the Walking Skeleton for Fleet: a real, runnable, end-to-end vertical slice in which a human types `fleet project add .` in a git repo and Fleet — a loopback-only Fastify daemon backed by a WAL-mode SQLite file it migrated itself — records the project and hands it back on `fleet project list`, surviving a daemon restart.

Purpose: Phase 1's success criteria 1 and 5 both hinge on this slice being real rather than layered. This plan proves the whole stack (Node 22 toolchain -> TypeScript strict -> Drizzle schema -> migration runner -> better-sqlite3 WAL -> registry module -> Fastify + zod route -> loopback bind -> HTTP CLI client) on one path before any expansion task widens it. Every later plan in this phase and every later phase inherits the architectural decisions made here.

Output: a working repo skeleton with `npm run dev` starting a daemon on `127.0.0.1:4177`, `npm test` green and hermetic, and `fleet project add|list` operating over HTTP only.
</objective>

<user_story>
**As a** solo developer running many git repos,
**I want to** register a repo with Fleet from my terminal and see it listed back,
**so that** Fleet has a durable, restart-surviving source of truth for where my projects live before it ever tries to run an agent against one.
</user_story>

Scaffold the single-package monorepo root. This is not an expansion task — it is the Wave-0 harness the tracer's `<automated>` verify cannot exist without, plus two pure primitives the tracer imports.

`.nvmrc` contains `22`. `package.json` sets `"type": "module"`, `"engines": { "node": ">=22" }`, `"bin": { "fleet": "./dist/cli/index.js" }`, and scripts: `dev` (`tsx src/cli/index.ts daemon`), `build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.json`), `test` (`vitest run --project unit`), `test:all` (`vitest run --project unit`), `spikes` (`vitest run --project spike`), `db:generate` (`drizzle-kit generate`), `lint`, `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`).

Install exactly these runtime dependencies at the versions verified in RESEARCH.md § Standard Stack: `fastify@5`, `better-sqlite3@13`, `drizzle-orm@0.45`, `zod@4`, `pino@10`, `fastify-type-provider-zod`, `commander`, `yaml`. Dev dependencies: `typescript@5`, `drizzle-kit@0.31`, `vitest@4`, `@types/node`, `tsx`, `eslint`, `typescript-eslint`, `prettier`, `execa@10`. Do NOT install `@types/better-sqlite3` — better-sqlite3 13.x ships its own types and the separate `@types` package is stale at the 7.x API surface. Every one of these packages carries an Approved disposition in RESEARCH.md § Package Legitimacy Audit; the `too-new` SUS flags there are a verified false positive of the checker's latest-publish-date heuristic, so no install checkpoint is warranted.

`tsconfig.json`: `"strict": true`, `"target": "ES2023"`, `"module": "NodeNext"`, `"moduleResolution": "NodeNext"`, `"outDir": "dist"`, `"rootDir": "src"`, `"noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true`, `"skipLibCheck": true`. This is the whole of QUAL-01's enforcement surface.

`vitest.config.ts`: write it fresh against the Vitest 4 API — do not adapt a v2/v3 snippet; `poolOptions`, `maxThreads`, `maxForks`, `singleThread` and `singleFork` were removed in v4 and `maxWorkers` replaces them. Define two named projects per D-11: project `unit` with `include: ['src/**/*.test.ts']` and `exclude: ['src/spikes/**']`, and project `spike` with `include: ['src/spikes/**/*.spike.test.ts']` and a `testTimeout` of 120000. The default `npm test` runs only `unit`, so it stays hermetic — no daemon, no real `claude` process.

`drizzle.config.ts`: `dialect: 'sqlite'`, `schema: './src/db/schema.ts'`, `out: './drizzle'`.

`.gitignore`: `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `*.db`, `*.db-wal`, `*.db-shm`, `.fleet-test/`.

`src/cli/exit-codes.ts` exports the four const numbers of D-19: `EXIT_OK = 0`, `EXIT_FAILED = 1`, `EXIT_USAGE = 2`, `EXIT_DAEMON_UNREACHABLE = 3`.

`src/config.ts` implements D-02 and D-03 as one module both the daemon and the CLI import, so the two can never disagree about where state lives or which port to use. Export `FLEET_DEFAULT_PORT = 4177`; `resolveFleetHome()` returning `process.env.FLEET_HOME` if set else `path.join(os.homedir(), '.fleet')`; `resolveDbPath()` returning `<fleetHome>/fleet.db`; `readConfigFile()` reading `<fleetHome>/config.json` and returning `{}` when the file is absent (an absent config file is the normal case, not an error) but throwing when it exists and is unparseable; `resolvePort()` applying the order `FLEET_PORT` env var, then the config file's `port` key, then `FLEET_DEFAULT_PORT`; and `resolveBaseUrl()` returning `http://127.0.0.1:${resolvePort()}`. No XDG split, one flat home directory.

`src/config.test.ts` covers the resolution order: env beats config file beats default, for both home and port; an absent config file yields the default port; a malformed config file throws.

  <behavior>
    - Against a temp git repo with an `origin` remote: `POST /projects {path}` returns 201 with `slug` derived from the directory name, `repo_path` absolute, `remote_url` from `git remote get-url origin`, `default_branch` from `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`.
    - Against a temp directory that is not a git repo: `POST /projects` returns 400 with body `{ error: { code: "not_a_git_repo", ... } }` and no row is inserted.
    - Against a temp git repo with no `origin` remote: `POST /projects` returns 201, `remote_url` is null, `default_branch` falls back to the local HEAD branch, and the response `warnings` array is non-empty.
    - Posting a second project whose slug collides with an existing non-archived project returns 409 with `{ error: { code: "slug_conflict", ... } }`.
    - `GET /projects` on an empty database returns `{ projects: [] }` with status 200.
    - `GET /projects` returns projects ordered by `created_at` ascending then `id` ascending, so ties break stably.
    - A remote URL carrying userinfo (`https://u:redacted@example.invalid/x/y.git`) is stored and returned with the userinfo stripped.
    - The CLI with no daemon listening exits with code 3 and prints a message naming the base URL.
    - After closing and reopening the daemon against the same `FLEET_HOME`, `GET /projects` still returns the previously registered project.
  </behavior>
